description: Make the frontend render the new backend tool events properly. frontend/src/tools.ts currently recognises only the pi tool names read/write/edit, so the read_file, write_file and patch_file events emitted by the new Hermes loop would fall through to the generic transient '🔧 {name}' status line instead of the labelled audit trail in the thread. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 and touches only the frontend.
steps: Read frontend/src/tools.ts, frontend/src/tools.test.ts and the 'tool' case of handleEvent in frontend/src/components/Chat.tsx (around lines 339-365) before editing.

In frontend/src/tools.ts, introduce two small name sets (read-like: 'read', 'read_file'; write-like: 'write', 'edit', 'write_file', 'patch_file') and use them in both isFileOp and toolLabel so the new names get the existing piChat.toolRead / piChat.toolWrite labels. Keep the existing behaviour for unnamed and unknown payloads untouched (the '🔧 outil…' regression guard must stay green).

In frontend/src/components/Chat.tsx, extend the jobWroteFiles.current condition so write_file and patch_file with status 'done' also mark the job as having written files, reusing the write-like set exported from tools.ts rather than duplicating the literals. Do NOT touch buildDeskPrompt, MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS or the file_changed handling.

Add cases to frontend/src/tools.test.ts asserting: isFileOp is true for {name:'read_file', path:'a.md'}, {name:'write_file', path:'a.md'} and {name:'patch_file', path:'a.md'}, and false when the path is empty; toolLabel returns '📄 Lecture de a.md' for read_file and '✏️ Écriture de a.md' for write_file and patch_file (fr bundle, same style as the existing assertions).

Add a Chat.test.tsx case in the existing style asserting that a tool event {name:'write_file', path:'B1/unit5.md', status:'done'} appears in the thread as a tool message (not only as the transient status line), and that {name:'file_changed', path:...} still triggers onFileChanged and is not displayed.
Verify by mutation: revert the tools.ts name sets to the old literals and confirm the new tools.test.ts and Chat.test.tsx assertions fail, then restore. Record which test caught it in findings.

Run npx vitest --run and npm run build, then commit with a conventional message such as 'feat: label read_file/write_file/patch_file tool events in the chat thread'. Do not push, do not touch version.json.
acceptance_criteria: cd frontend && npx vitest --run passes, including the new assertions, with the pre-existing 79 tests still green
cd frontend && npm run build succeeds
isFileOp returns true for read_file, write_file and patch_file when a path is present, and toolLabel gives them the existing read/write labels in fr and en
A write_file tool event with status done is rendered as a tool message in the thread and marks jobWroteFiles
findings:
Implemented in tools.ts as two exported sets, READ_TOOL_NAMES = {read, read_file} and WRITE_TOOL_NAMES = {write, edit, write_file, patch_file}, used by isFileOp and toolLabel; Chat.tsx imports WRITE_TOOL_NAMES for the jobWroteFiles.current condition instead of duplicating the literals. toolLabel now tests tool.path first, then set membership, so the no-name payload still lands on piChat.toolUnknown ('🔧 outil…' guard stays green). Chat.test.tsx: renderConnected's props type gained an optional onFileChanged so the new test can assert the synthetic file_changed event; FEAT-004 should keep that. Verification: frontend npx vitest --run = 8 files / 84 tests passing (79 pre-existing + 5 new), npm run build ok; backend go build/vet/test ok and gofmt printed nothing (untouched). Mutation test (sets reverted to the old literals ['read'] and ['write','edit'], backup kept inside the repo as src/tools.ts.mutbak and restored in the same shell command because /tmp does not persist): exactly the 5 new assertions failed, the 79 pre-existing stayed green. Failing tests were tools.test.ts 'labels the Hermes file tools like the pi ones', 'labels the Hermes file tools in en too', 'is true for the Hermes file tools when they carry a path', and Chat.test.tsx 'keeps a write_file event in the thread and marks the answer as having written files' + 'keeps a read_file event in the thread'. The write_file Chat test also covers jobWroteFiles by asserting the answer renders 'Fichier mis à jour par Pi.' and no Insert button. buildDeskPrompt, MAX_INLINED_FILE_CHARS, bridge/pi.go and LyaChat.tsx untouched. Note for FEAT-004: the 'file updated' note reuses the pi wording piChat.updated, which mentions Pi even when Lya wrote the file - worth a dedicated string when the direct-update sub-mode lands.

REVIEW PASS v1 (2025-08-24-200500-review.md) — tool-event rendering dispositions, all FIXED, each mutation-verified:
- Issue 2 (tool errors rendered as successes): FIXED. NormalizedTool now carries `error` (and `outsideWorkingFile`), and toolLabel branches on status === 'error' before the read/write labels, so a refused patch reads "⚠️ Échec sur B1/unite1.md : old_string introuvable" instead of "✏️ Écriture de B1/unite1.md". jobWroteFiles still keys on status === 'done', so a refusal leaves the Insert button rather than the "Fichier mis à jour par Lya." note. New i18n keys piChat.toolFailed / toolFailedNoPath / toolErrorGeneric in fr.json and en.json. Tests: tools.test.ts (label with and without path, missing reason, en) and Chat.test.tsx 'renders a refused write as an error, not as a write'.
- Issue 3 (malformed arguments leave no trace): FIXED. isFileOp keeps a known file tool in the thread when it has a path OR failed, so the error event of a call whose arguments could not be decoded (no path at all) is an audit line instead of a transient status that vanishes. An unrelated tool failing still goes to the status line. Tests: tools.test.ts 'keeps a failed file tool in the thread even without a path', Chat.test.tsx 'keeps a trace of a tool call whose arguments could not be decoded'.
- Issue 6, frontend half: the backend's "outsideWorkingFile": true flag is appended to the thread label as "⚠️ hors du fichier de travail affiché" (chat.outsideWorkingFile, fr + en), so the banner's promise and the actual write cannot silently disagree. Tests: Chat.test.tsx 'flags a write that landed outside the announced working file' / 'does not flag a write on the announced working file'.
- Follow-up on the earlier FEAT-003 finding about piChat.updated: already resolved in FEAT-004, which introduced chat.updated ("Fichier mis à jour par Lya."). Unchanged here.


REVIEW v2 (2025-08-24-202600-review.md, commit 66855db) — tool-event rendering:
- tools.ts exports isToolRunning(tool) (status 'running' from both bridges, 'started' from Hermes progress frames) and toolLabel gained in-progress variants piChat.toolReading / piChat.toolWriting (fr + en). Chat.tsx routes a running file op to the transient status line and only appends the terminal event to the thread, then clears the status line. Before, the pre-execution event was rendered with the completed-write label: every operation appeared twice and a refused write was preceded by '✏️ Écriture de X'. Note this also fixes mode Pi, which emits the same running/done pair (pi.go tool_execution_start/end).
- New tests: Chat.test.tsx 'shows a write as in progress, and in the thread only once it is over' and 'never shows a refused write as a completed one, not even for an instant'; tools.test.ts 'is true only before the terminal event' and 'labels a running file tool as in progress, in fr and en'. Mutation-verified (running events appended again; isToolRunning forced to false).
